newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, September 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, September 27.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Majority party leaders found an agreement over the 1997 budget which is going to contain 50 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures. These include an additional "tax for Europe" on revenues to be paid in 1997. Pensions and healthcare will not be sharply cut, so contenting hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti (all).
* The Freedom alliance will oppose the budget in parliament. "The government is held hostage by Bertinotti" (all).
* State railway managing director Lorenzo Necci, arrested and jailed in corruption probe, has resigned (all).
* Generali, Italy's largest insurer, reported a 11.7 pct fall in first half 1996 profits as it suffered from a stronger lira (Sole 24 Ore).
* Tyre and cable group Pirelli posted a near-doubling of first half profits : consolidated net profits rose to 206 billion lire from 115 billion (Sole 24 Ore).
*Metal workers stage national strike today over the renewal of their contracts (all).
* Finnish Nokia Telecommunications is interested in providing the digital network for a third mobile phones operator in Italy (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
